_comment: Per-character settings. target_height is metres from floor to helmet top; the TRELLIS sources are unit height. facing_deg rotates the source about the vertical axis so it faces the game's -Z (Blender +Y). Landmarks are fractions of height/width auto-detected by process.py; any value set under 'landmark_overrides' wins. 'classes' maps material classes to physically based [roughness, metallic] targets; the original TRELLIS roughness/metal variation is kept around each target (see process.py classify). pad_width (fraction of height) keeps shoulder armour on the torso when arms are cut for the rig.

known_issues: TRELLIS textures carry no emissive data, so no light strips glow
2K base colour spread over thousands of tiny UV charts: soft at close range (no upscaling applied)
rigid-segment rig (the game's animation system), not a skinned mesh: small seams can show at bent joints
T-pose arms are bent down at the shoulder procedurally after baking; hands keep TRELLIS's open-hand shape
TRELLIS predicted ~0.66 metallic on painted plates; re-derived per class
brass/gold accents are mostly too small or dark to classify (0.02% of texels)

bathysphere.landmark_notes: Legs are bridged near the knees in the TRELLIS mesh, so the centre-line crotch detector reports 33% of height; values set from the reference artwork (crotch ~47-48%).
